articles.fullText:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
The following is the full text of Xi's toast at the banquet:
Dear Colleagues,
Distinguished Guests,
Ladies and Gentlemen,
Dear Friends,
Good evening.
Tonight, the shores of the South China Sea are ablaze with light, and Shenzhen is at its autumn best. On the eve of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, I wish to extend, on behalf of the Chinese government and the Chinese people, our warmest welcome to all distinguished guests.
I have often said that to see over a few thousand years of China, go to Xi'an; to see 500 years of China, go to Beijing; to see 100 years of China, go to Shanghai. Tonight, let me add this: To see 50 years of China, come to Shenzhen.
Shenzhen is a place with a big story to tell. When I first set foot here in 1978, it was little more than a fishing village. In the blink of an eye, more than four decades have passed. Today, high-rises stretch across the horizon and traffic surges through the streets—a transformation nothing short of miraculous.
Openness is in Shenzhen's DNA. From a remote border town to an international metropolis, from merely attracting foreign capital and technology to actively helping shape international rules – Shenzhen today has trade links spanning the globe and welcomes an endless stream of businesspeople and travelers. It stands as a window on China's high-standard opening up.
Innovation is the wellspring of Shenzhen's vitality. From export processing to independent research and development, from "world factory" to "city of innovation" – Shenzhen today files up to 20,000 international patent applications a year. Advanced manufacturing and modern services flourish side by side, placing the city at the forefront of China's cluster-based innovation.
Cooperation is the source of Shenzhen's strength. As the people of Shenzhen like to say, "Once here, Shenzhener forever." The city opens its minds and arms to go-getters from around the world and brings together talent from over 100 countries and regions, making it a vibrant hub of win-win cooperation between China and the rest of the world.
The Shenzhen story is a microcosm of China's reform and opening up. Generation after generation of builders have started from scratch and worked tirelessly to blaze new trails. They have forged ahead in reform and opening up, unleashed and developed the productive forces, and showcased the great dynamism of Chinese modernization.
The Shenzhen story is also a shining example of Asia-Pacific cooperation. Economies across the region have risen above geographic constraints and differences in thinking, thrown themselves into the wide arena of regional cooperation, and created the Asia-Pacific miracle of rapid economic growth.
Since its founding, APEC has always been known for openness, innovation and cooperation. From the first handshake in Seattle to the historic gathering by Beijing's Yanqi Lake, from the solemn commitment to the Bogor Goals to the broad vision of building an Asia-Pacific community – APEC has remained attuned to the pulse of our times, spearheaded economic integration in the Asia-Pacific, and helped make this region the most dynamic in the global economy and a vital engine of world growth.
"On separate sails, we give our best; even a thousand miles apart, the same wind connects our quest." This verse captures perfectly why we have crossed mountains and seas to come together – united by the shared purpose of building an Asia-Pacific community. Since becoming the APEC Chair, China has hosted over 300 meetings and events across 16 cities in the course of the year, with more than 10,000 delegates from member economies taking part and helping to deliver significant outcomes during the APEC China Year. At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss steps to expand mutual openness, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, extend opportunities for result-oriented cooperation across various fields, and strive to deliver more tangible results on the ground. I look forward to discussing with you the great endeavor of Asia-Pacific cooperation and advancing our shared cause of Asia-Pacific development.

(ECNS) -- The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum has long promoted free and open trade and investment, helping foster regional growth and shared prosperity, U.S. business leaders told China News Service during a series of APEC meetings in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, from Nov. 16 to 20.
They described APEC as a forum for facilitating regional trade and strengthening policy coordination. They called for closer China-U.S. cooperation in areas such as digital payments and paperless trade to support growth across the Asia-Pacific.
Michael Hart, president of the American Chamber of Commerce in China, said the meetings brings business executives and government leaders together.
For U.S. companies, the meetings offer a chance to better understand China's long-term market prospects and identify business opportunities, he said.
Hart also said enterprises are focusing on opportunities and innovation in China, including the rise of young, competitive Chinese companies in emerging industries.
"One of the things happening in Shenzhen is a good example of how fast China has changed and innovated. We've got the headquarters of a number of Chinese companies here and it really shows the innovation going on in China," he said.
Hart noted that many U.S. companies operate in Shenzhen and elsewhere in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.
"It's important for U.S. companies to have clear rules from both sides from their home country and also from China so they understand the environment they can operate in," he said.
Sean Stein, president of the U.S.-China Business Council (USCBC), said APEC's significance extended beyond China-U.S. ties to the entire Asia-Pacific region. One of its main goals was to make the cross-border movement of goods smoother and more efficient, he said.
He cited high-tech products such as robots, noting that their components could cross borders multiple times, moving through China, Malaysia, Vietnam, Singapore and the United States before returning to China.
"The more complex the supply chain, the more important APEC becomes," he said.
Stein said progress through APEC would be gradual. "What we'll see coming out of APEC are many small, incremental changes and recommendations that add up to a great deal in the aggregate."
Shenzhen companies stand to benefit substantially from APEC efforts to make trade easier and more efficient. The gains would extend to economies across APEC and consumers around the world, he said.
The U.S. business leaders also stressed that closer cooperation with China would strengthen bilateral trade and support wider regional cooperation and growth.
Stein said APEC could better achieve its goals with China and the U.S. working together. Digital payments and paperless trade were among the areas where the two sides could make progress.
"Think about how many times goods cross borders every single second in APEC. These little steps are going to make every single one of those transactions a little bit easier, cheaper, faster, and more efficient, but the real impact is going to come from the U.S. and China working together on this and that's what we expect to see out of APEC."
Hart identified sustainability, supply chains and economic resilience as priority areas for China-U.S. cooperation. China's market and continued innovation offered companies in both countries opportunities to work together, he said.
Agriculture is another key part of China-U.S. trade. Carlos Salinas, executive director for East Asia at the U.S. Soybean Export Council (USSEC), said China remained a key market for U.S. soybeans and that American farmers hoped to keep selling there.
U.S. companies in other sectors also see opportunities in China's growth. Having operated in China for more than four decades, HP continues to look for ways to expand its business.
Brittany Masalosalo, chief public policy officer at HP Inc., said China is an important part of HP's global manufacturing supply chain and a major hub for research, development and innovation. She said talent from Chinese universities and an active community of local innovators create opportunities for partnerships with multinational companies.

In international politics, the significance of a meeting is not always measured by the agreements reached, but sometimes by who are gathered around the table.
When Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump sit down together in Shenzhen on Thursday, it will mark the first trilateral meeting among the leaders of the three major powers.
The meeting will be held against the backdrop of conflict in many corners of the world, disruptions to energy supplies and supply chains, and excitement and concerns over new technologies and their regulation. Bringing the three leaders together creates an opportunity to communicate on issues that extend well beyond bilateral relationships.
This does not mean the three countries will reach sweeping agreements or find common ground on every issue. However, the Shenzhen meeting is expected to establish a channel for strategic communication between the three powers, help reduce confrontation and improve their ability to manage differences.
While the symbolism of the three leaders meeting together is high, analysts reject comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the United States, the Soviet Union and Britain negotiated key arrangements for the postwar world.
What's on the agenda?
An official agenda for the trilateral meeting has not been announced, but the Chinese Foreign Ministry has said it will be of "groundbreaking significance" and will promote world peace and enable "strategic stability" of major countries.
This suggests a focus on opening up communication channels in order to cooperate on issues of common concern and explore ways to lay foundations for enhancing stability in various areas.
The leaders could touch on strategic weapons and how to manage the risks they pose, without following the model of formal, treaty-based arms control negotiations seen in the 20th century.
On regional conflicts, any progress would require the participation of the parties directly involved, but the meeting could still help establish a framework for addressing such issues in future discussions.
On regulation of new technologies, there could be an opportunity for the three sides to seek potential points of convergence.
In this sense, the consequence of the gathering may lie less in any immediate agreements than in whether it paves the way for continued high-level engagement among China, Russia and the US in the longer term.
The significance of trilateral engagement becomes clearer when viewed against the very different trajectories of the three countries' respective bilateral relationships.
China and Russia have developed a comprehensive strategic partnership, or lately the "China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for a new era," underpinned by regular high-level exchanges and expanding cooperation in areas including trade, energy, industry and technology. Xi and Putin met in China in May and again on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in August, reaffirming their commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation.
China-US relations, meanwhile, are being managed through renewed high-level engagement and economic dialogue, even as competition over technology and unresolved trade issues continue to test the relationship. Xi and Trump have met twice this year – in Beijing in May and Washington in September – and agreed to pursue a constructive relationship of strategic stability.
The relationship between Russia and the US has followed a different trajectory. Trump has sought to engage Putin directly and revive negotiations over the conflict in Ukraine, but diplomatic efforts have yet to bridge major differences over the terms of a settlement. Recent contacts between US envoys and Putin, followed by talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, have highlighted both Washington's willingness to pursue diplomacy and the obstacles that remain.
The question, then, is whether these separate bilateral dynamics can translate into a broader understanding among the three powers on issues that affect them all.

在周日于宝山区举行的2026吴淞口论坛上，行业代表强调了将该港口从邮轮母港转型为连接江河与海洋运输的综合枢纽，同时培育更广泛邮轮产业生态的愿景。作为中国邮轮产业的重要门户，吴淞口国际邮轮港连续多年保持在中国邮轮市场的领先地位。根据宝山区人民政府的数据，2026年前三季度，该港口的邮轮靠泊艘次和出入境旅客流量分别占全国总量的55%和76%。国际旅客的日益增多也成为其运营的一个显著特点。3月28日，一次近5900名注册旅客的到访创下了该码头单日入境外国旅客人数的新纪录。

国际邮轮旅客的增长正值中国扩大免签入境政策和促进入境旅游之际。邮轮旅行也正成为海外游客探索中国的重要渠道，上海则是连接国际旅客与更多目的地的主要门户。
